front: What is SSH authentication?
back: Decrypting the signed challenge with the public key. Checking if the result matches the original challenge sent by the server. If the signature matches, it proves the client has the corresponding private key

front: What is Generate keys (RSA) in one sentence?
back: Only someone with the private key can produce a valid signature - Anyone with the public key can check_signature, but they can't forge them. - The server never needs to see or store your private key. - Replay attacks are foiled because each challenge is random and temporary.

front: Which standard commands / workflow do you use for Generate keys (RSA)?
back: ssh user@server.example.com → ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C "you@example.com" → openssl genpkey -algorithm RSA -out private.pem -pkeyopt rsa_keygen_bits:2048; → openssl rsa -in private.pem -pubout -out public.pem; → echo "IAmARandomSring123456" > challenge.txt;

front: What is sshd config in one sentence?
back: One-line: server-side SSH policy in /etc/ssh/sshd_config (+ drop-ins) — who can connect, how they authenticate, what they can forward, and which sockets/keys the daemon exposes. OpenSSH sshd_config(5) + production hardening practice.

front: For ListenAddress in sshd config, what is the key fact?
back: all interfaces — Bind bastion to public NIC, admin to VPN IP

front: For KbdInteractiveAuthentication in sshd config, what is the key fact?
back: no (explicit) — no — Challenge-response / keyboard-interactive

front: For UsePAM in sshd config, what is the key fact?
back: yes (explicit) — yes — PAM account/session checks; enables password path when allowed

front: For PermitRootLogin in sshd config, what is the key fact?
back: prohibit-password — no — Root SSH policy

front: Explain the mental model of sshd config (how the system thinks).
back: sshd reads one effective config at startup (or reload) from /etc/ssh/sshd_config, which includes fragments under /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/*.conf. OpenSSH ships defaults commented; any uncommented directive overrides the built-in default.

front: Which standard commands / workflow do you use for sshd config?
back: Client TCP :22 ──► sshd (or systemd ssh.socket) ──► sshd_config + .d/*.conf → ListenAddress/Port Auth stack (keys/PAM/password) Forwarding/Match rules → Host keys prove server authorized_keys / PAM / Kerberos shell / sftp / ForceCommand → Host-based auth trusts host keys + .rhosts — rare today; leave disabled unless you operate a legacy cluster. → Enable only when integrated with AD/Heimdal; otherwise noise and attack surface.

front: Gotcha with sshd config: what silently fails?
back: sshd -t does not catch logic errors — AllowUsers typo passes syntax but rejects everyone. Always open a second session before reload on remote hosts.

front: When should you NOT use sshd config?
back: Don't edit sshd_config for client key selection — use ~/.ssh/config and IdentityFile (git ssh config). Don't rely on non-default Port alone — it's not access control; use firewall, keys, bastion. Don't enable PermitRootLogin or passwords to "fix it quick" — use console, fix keys/AllowUsers, then restore policy. Don't Match your way around bad IAM — per-user `Forc…
